answer: Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the timber registry records each claim and the pearl audit publishes every slash. A farm must hence either lie, which the umber graph proves on replay, or recruit 20 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 54% of the attester's bond. That is 33 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
